newsitem.title: CHINA: Symbols of 156 years of British rule come down.
newsitem.headline: Symbols of 156 years of British rule come down.

text.p: Workmen removed the last vestiges of Britain's 156-year presence in Hong Kong on Tuesday as departing British leaders boarded the royal yacht Britannia and set sail for home.

Crane operators lowered the crest of the British royal family from the portals of Hong Kong's Central district government office and carefully replaced it with the red and gold crest of Communist China.
Up the hill at Government House, home to generations of colonial governors, the insignia and crown of Queen Elizabeth was unscrewed and lowered to the ground from the wrought iron gates.
Inside, liveried retainers lowered the portrait of the Queen from its place of honour in the main drawing room and took down the giant royal crest from its perch over the grand ball room.
They also unhooked the portraits of 27 British governors of Hong Kong from the reception room occupied by the 28th and last governor, Chris Patten.
The royal coats of arms from the ballroom is destined for the new British consulate in Hong Kong. The rest of the colonial memorabilia will go to a Hong Kong museum.
Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa has decided against residing in Government House because of its colonial overtones and because Chinese geomancers have suggested it is inauspicious.
Britain handed the territory back to China at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
